$comment: Routing judgements, not benchmark claims. Re-check profiles when a new family ships. Every task class must stay reachable, or `check` fails.

tiers.$comment: Capability bands. minTier is the weakest band that reliably finishes a task unattended.

capabilities.$comment: Model-side flags. Tasks require them, profiles declare them; `check` keeps both aligned.
capabilities.multiFileEdit: Can hold a change plan across several files and apply it consistently.
capabilities.longHorizonPlanning: Can own a multi-step task for many tool calls without losing the goal.
capabilities.deepReasoning: Reliable on ambiguous architecture, root-cause and trade-off analysis.
capabilities.toolUse: Calls tools with well-formed arguments and recovers from tool errors.
capabilities.codeExecution: Writes and runs code/commands and interprets the result.
capabilities.longContext: Comfortable reading large diffs, logs and many files in one pass.
capabilities.vision: Can read screenshots, diagrams and rendered UI.
capabilities.structuredOutput: Produces strict JSON/YAML matching a requested schema.

harnessCapabilities.$comment: Tool-side flags. false is a hard block; "unknown" means verify before promising.
harnessCapabilities.imageGeneration: Has an image generation or editing tool.
harnessCapabilities.shell: Can run shell commands in the workspace.
harnessCapabilities.previewServer: Can expose a long-running server as a live preview.
harnessCapabilities.githubWrite: Can create or merge PRs, issues and releases.
harnessCapabilities.gitPush: Can push branches to the remote.

detection.$comment: Checked in order; first non-empty wins. High confidence only if it names the model.

profiles.$comment: Longest literal run wins, so `*gpt-5-mini*` beats `*gpt-5*`. Match families, not versions.

fallbackProfile.$comment: Used when nothing matches or nothing was reported. Assume the least and ask.
fallbackProfile.label: Unidentified model

taskClasses.$comment: requires = model flags, requiresHarness = tool flags, guardrails = conditions even when allowed. Omit minTier if any model can do it.

multi-file-refactor.label: Multi-file refactor
suitableExamples: split a service into a controller, service and repository
rename a config key across packages and update every call site
move a shared type into @n8n/api-types
unsuitableExamples: rewrite the whole editor-ui state layer
refactor packages/core while the model cannot run tests
guardrails: Land the change in reviewable slices; never leave the tree unbuildable between slices.
Run typecheck and the affected package's tests before claiming done.
alternatives: Do one package or one symbol per turn and confirm each slice.
Hand off to a frontier model with this scope statement.

architecture-design.label: Architecture and design decisions
suitableExamples: decide where a new execution hook belongs
compare two migration strategies for a table
design the boundary between the editor and the AI assistant
unsuitableExamples: invent a new database engine
guess at infrastructure the repo does not document
guardrails: State assumptions and cite the files that support them.
Prefer the existing pattern in @n8n/api-types, @n8n/di and @n8n/config.
alternatives: Ask for a written spec first (n8n:spec-driven-development), then implement the agreed part.

bug-root-cause.label: Bug root-cause analysis
suitableExamples: find why a node returns a 429 wrapped as a success
trace a stack frame into the shared execution boundary
unsuitableExamples: guess a cause from the error title alone
diagnose a bug that needs the reporter's private data
guardrails: Separate observed evidence from inference in the answer.
Reproduce or state exactly why reproduction was not possible.
alternatives: Run n8n:reproduce-bug to narrow the boundary mechanically.
Collect one more piece of evidence and stop rather than guessing.

unit-test-authoring.label: Unit and integration tests
suitableExamples: add a vitest case for a retry helper
write a regression test that injects a provider error
unsuitableExamples: assert on a snapshot nobody reviewed
add a test that needs real third-party credentials
guardrails: Tests must fail for the right reason before the fix and pass after it.
Run the test file, not a broader suite, to keep feedback tight.
alternatives: Write the test skeleton and mark the assertion as a TODO for review.

node-integration.label: New integration node
suitableExamples: scaffold a node with credentials, an operation and an icon
add an operation to an existing node
unsuitableExamples: invent API endpoints that are not documented
hardcode a token into credentials defaults
guardrails: Follow n8n:node-add-oauth for auth and the community-node lint rules.
Never invent endpoint shapes; cite the provider documentation.
alternatives: Scaffold from an existing similar node and leave API calls unimplemented.

db-migration.label: Database migration
suitableExamples: add a nullable column with a backfill
add an index for a slow query
unsuitableExamples: drop a column that still has readers
rewrite migration history
guardrails: Use n8n:db-migrations; keep sqlite and postgres paths in sync.
Run pnpm db:schema:check:sqlite.
Never make a destructive change without an explicit instruction.
alternatives: Propose the migration in a doc and let a human apply it.

security-review.label: Security review
suitableExamples: review a diff for authz gaps before it merges
check that a new endpoint is protected (n8n:protect-endpoints)
unsuitableExamples: publish a write-up of an unpatched vulnerability
promise that code is secure
guardrails: This repo is public: keep the vector out of branch names, PR titles, tests and comments.
Report findings privately per SECURITY.md; never open a public issue for a live vulnerability.
alternatives: Summarize risk areas for a human security reviewer without exploit detail.

large-context-triage.label: Large log or diff triage
suitableExamples: cluster 2000 failing test cases into causes
read a 4000-line diff and list only behaviour changes
unsuitableExamples: paste the whole repository into one prompt
summarize a log you have not actually loaded
guardrails: Read files in targeted ranges; quote line numbers.
Stop and ask for the missing artifact instead of inventing its contents.
alternatives: Filter with grep/rg first and triage a smaller slice.

visual-ui-review.label: Screenshot and UI review
suitableExamples: compare a component against the design-system rules
read an error screenshot and locate the failing widget
unsuitableExamples: judge spacing from a description without the image
claim pixel accuracy you cannot measure
guardrails: Ask for the screenshot or render it yourself; describe what is visible, not what is likely.
Check n8n:design-system rules before proposing visual changes.
alternatives: Review the DOM and CSS instead of the pixels.

web-research.label: Current web research
suitableExamples: check the current provider API for a rate-limit header
confirm whether a CVE affects a dependency
unsuitableExamples: recall a 2024 API shape from memory and present it as current
fetch an internal dashboard without credentials
guardrails: Cite the source, and say when the only sources are the model's training data.
Prefer official docs over blog posts.
alternatives: Ask the user to paste the page or the relevant snippet.

image-generation.label: Image generation or editing
suitableExamples: make a placeholder hero image for docs
clean up a screenshot for a PR description
unsuitableExamples: generate a company logo and call it final
recreate a proprietary asset
guardrails: Treat generated assets as drafts; never overwrite a tracked brand asset.
Keep generated binaries out of Git unless the task requires them.
alternatives: Hand off to an image-capable tool or ask the user for the asset.

audio-transcription.label: Audio transcription
suitableExamples: summarize a recorded bug walkthrough
unsuitableExamples: transcribe a file you cannot open
guardrails: Quote timestamps; do not paraphrase decisions as verbatim text.
alternatives: Ask for a transcript or a loom link (n8n:loom-transcript).

mechanical-bulk-edit.label: Mechanical bulk edit / codemod
suitableExamples: rename a test helper everywhere
apply one lint autofix across a package
unsuitableExamples: change behaviour while claiming it is mechanical
guardrails: Drive it with a script or a codemod, not hand edits.
Show the diff stat and run the affected tests.
alternatives: Do ten files by hand and confirm the pattern before scaling.

commit-and-pr-text.label: Commit messages, PR bodies, release notes
suitableExamples: write a PR body from the diff (n8n:create-pr)
turn merged PRs into release notes
unsuitableExamples: describe a fix you did not verify
mention a customer name in a public artifact
guardrails: Describe what the code now does; follow .github/pull_request_title_conventions.md.
Keep security vectors and customer names out — this repo is public.
alternatives: Draft the skeleton and let the author fill in the unknowns.

translation-and-copy.label: i18n strings and UI copy
suitableExamples: add a new UI string across locales
tighten a tooltip
unsuitableExamples: invent a locale key format
edit generated i18n files by hand
guardrails: All UI text goes through i18n ($t('key')); never hardcode English in components.
Match the tone rules in n8n:content-design.
alternatives: Propose the English string and let a translator review the rest.

dependency-upgrade.label: Dependency upgrade
suitableExamples: bump a major version and fix the breakage
unsuitableExamples: upgrade five majors at once
edit the lockfile by hand
guardrails: One dependency per change; read the changelog before editing.
Run build, typecheck and tests; do not hand-edit pnpm-lock.yaml.
alternatives: Open an issue with the upgrade plan and a reproduction of the breakage.

flaky-test-investigation.label: Flaky test investigation
suitableExamples: find the race in an e2e that fails 1 in 20 runs
unsuitableExamples: add a retry and call it fixed
guardrails: Prove the flake with repeated runs before changing the test.
Report the observed failure rate, not an impression.
alternatives: Quarantine the test with a tracking issue instead of guessing.

pr-merge.label: Merging or closing a pull request
suitableExamples: merge #1234 with --squash after checks pass
unsuitableExamples: merge a PR to unblock yourself
use --auto to merge later
guardrails: Merge only on an explicit instruction, with the PR number, and never --auto.
The merge/close command must be the last command in the chain so its exit code is real.
alternatives: Leave the PR ready and report its status for a human to merge.

git-push.label: Pushing branches and opening PRs
suitableExamples: push the session branch and open a draft PR
unsuitableExamples: force-push master
push to another agent's branch
rewrite shared history
guardrails: Push only the session branch; never create or switch branches in an agent session.
Use gh pr create --draft unless told otherwise.
alternatives: Leave the commits local and hand the branch name to the user.

deterministic-computation.label: Arithmetic, dates, parsing, hashing
suitableExamples: convert a timestamp and a timezone
count lines in a CSV and sum a column
unsuitableExamples: estimate a checksum from memory
guardrails: Use a script or shell command for the answer; do not do it mentally.
Show the command and its output.
alternatives: Give the command for the user to run.

secret-handling.label: Handling credentials or secrets
suitableExamples: explain how to set an env var without printing it
unsuitableExamples: paste an API key into chat
commit a .env with a token
print a secret to debug a request
guardrails: Never request, echo, store or commit credentials; pass values via environment variables.
Never ask the user for a password, token or 2FA code.
alternatives: Tell the user where to set the variable and how to verify it is present without printing it.
Move the missing value into the harness's secret store.

legal-and-licensing.label: Legal or licence interpretation
suitableExamples: point to LICENSE.md and docs.n8n.io for the Sustainable Use License
unsuitableExamples: decide whether a use case is permitted by the licence
advise on a customer contract
guardrails: Summarize what the file says and route the decision to a human.
alternatives: Quote the licence section and ask legal@n8n.io.

unauthorized-mutation.label: Mutating external systems without authorization
suitableExamples: draft the change and show the diff
unsuitableExamples: apply a production migration
post to Linear or close issues because the session started
delete a customer's workflow
guardrails: Default to read-only; mutations need an explicit, specific instruction.
Draft comments and state changes until the user authorizes posting.
alternatives: Produce the exact command or payload for the user to run.

fabricated-evidence.label: Reporting results that were not observed
suitableExamples: say the test suite was not run and why
unsuitableExamples: claim a test passed without running it
invent a stack trace or a file that does not exist
summarize a document you never opened
guardrails: Distinguish observed from inferred in every report.
If a command could not run, say so and show the error.
alternatives: Run the check now, or hand back an explicit list of what remains unverified.
